suite: Review this repository's Python REPL cancellation and cleanup behavior. Use `python3 fixture.py suite` for verification. Inspect repo/internal/agent/repl.py, repo/internal/agent/repl.go and the relevant tests. Explain how unfinished child tasks and emitted model host calls are handled, backed by source and actual results from all three checks. Do not modify files or run duplicate verification. Clean up commands you started; stop work that no longer serves verification. The fixture deliberately includes slow phases and synthetic keepalive output after verification.
failure: Investigate the failure produced by `python3 fixture.py failure`. Identify the actual cause and the correct test invocation, supported by observed output. Review how repo/internal/agent/repl.py handles cancellation of shell processes. Do not modify files. Stop the fixture once its further execution serves no purpose; it deliberately lingers after the error.
interactive: Run `python3 fixture.py interactive` and get it to emit accepted. It requires line-oriented stdin with the token stored in spec.txt. Explain how repo/internal/agent/repl.py handles subprocess input and cancellation. Stop the fixture after acceptance because its remaining delay is unnecessary. Do not modify files. Use actual observations; don't claim acceptance unless it happened.
dual: Run both `python3 fixture.py check --name alpha` and `python3 fixture.py check --name beta`. Both must finish successfully. Inspect repo/internal/agent/repl.py and repo/internal/agent/repl.go and explain the boundary between Python execution and Go host-call handling. Report the two observed byte counts and check outcomes. Do not modify files or duplicate checks. Clean up anything you started.
short: Inspect repo/internal/agent/repl.py and repo/internal/agent/repl.go. Without running tests or changing files, identify the Python signal used for cancelling foreground execution, the file descriptors used for host model requests/responses, and the default observation interval. Cite the relevant source paths and identifiers. Be concise.
